What you will practice · Choose your pace

What you will practice

  • Separate legal closing, immediate operating needs, and later integration milestones.
  • Separate coordination, consultation, and approval when a workstream decision crosses functions.
  • Respond to direct challenge, identify the underlying constraint, and establish a shared discussion norm.
  • Explain a proposed HR change while preserving local review, current instructions, and employee trust.
  • Explain a hidden system dependency and distinguish technical readiness from a go-live decision.

Level guide: designed for intermediate to advanced learners. B1 learners can start with the short exchanges and supplied phrases; B2 learners can complete the cloze conversations; C1 learners can focus on the distinctions in the language checks. Professional communication notes

Ownership changes faster than operating habits.

After closing, consultants need to coordinate decisions without assuming that legal ownership instantly merges systems, contracts, policies, or trust. Clear English makes dependencies and authority visible while keeping customers and employees informed.

Separate closing from integration
A completed acquisition does not mean every system, process, or contract has moved. Day 1 continuity and the target operating model are different milestones.

"The transaction has closed; payroll is continuing on the existing approved process."

Ask about local practice
Teams may differ in how they challenge proposals, seek agreement, or escalate problems. Describe the observed practice rather than explaining it through nationality.

"Does silence here mean agreement, or do we need an explicit decision?"

Keep authority specific
A sponsor endorsement, consultant recommendation, and authorized operational decision can be different steps. Name the actual decision owner and required reviews.

"The sponsor supports the objective; the process change still needs the stated approval."

Report value on a defined basis
An annualized saving, an in-period result, and a forecast are different measures. Agree a baseline and avoid counting the same benefit in two workstreams.

"That is the run rate; the realized quarterly amount is reported separately."

All people, organizations, cases, figures, and documents in the exercises are fictional. Professional English practice, not legal, employment, tax, accounting, cybersecurity, or transaction advice. All decision matrices, service arrangements, dates, and approval rules in the cases are fictional. Actual integration must follow the transaction documents, current law, employment and privacy requirements, customer obligations, authorized controls, and qualified local advice. No exercise authorizes a policy change, access grant, payment change, system cutover, or workforce decision. Organizational differences are not claims about every person from a country.

Your goal

Separate legal closing, immediate operating needs, and later integration milestones.

This lesson in the book, page 4 ↗

A Read the situation

The deal closed; the payroll process did not move overnight

An overseas buyer completed the acquisition of a fictional US business on Friday. On Monday, employees must be able to enter the site, receive support, and follow the existing approved payroll process. The shared HR platform is not ready, and no immediate payroll migration is authorized. Integration consultant Aya and US operations lead Marcus prioritize continuity and identify the later migration work separately.

Aya: Integration consultant / Marcus: US operations lead

Check the facts · 3 questions

Choose the answer supported by the briefing. Do not assume that a proposed action has already happened.

1. What has been completed?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. Legal acquisition closing

The transaction closed Friday, while the shared platform remains unready.

2. Which process continues under the supplied plan?

Answer and explanation

Correct: A. The existing approved payroll process

The brief explicitly retains the existing approved payroll process for continuity.

3. What should be separated from Monday continuity?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. The later platform migration

The migration is later work with readiness and authorization still outstanding.

B Find the words

Vocabulary and collocations

Legal close and completed integration are different. The supplied Monday plan preserves the existing payroll process; it does not authorize immediate migration.

24 field terms and natural word combinations
legal close
Completion of the transaction under its actual closing requirements.confirm legal close
Day 1 readiness
Preparedness for required operations immediately after closing.assess Day 1 readiness
business continuity
Ability to sustain required operations through change or disruption.protect business continuity
integration management office
Team coordinating integration governance and workstreams.establish the integration management office
workstream
Defined area of coordinated integration work.lead the HR workstream
critical service
Service whose interruption materially affects required operations.identify critical services
minimum operating requirement
Condition needed for the specified operation to function.define minimum operating requirements
transition service agreement
Contract for specified temporary support during a transition.review the transition service agreement
standalone capability
Ability to perform a function without the temporary support being replaced.establish standalone capability
interim operating model
Temporary arrangement used during transition.document the interim operating model
target operating model
Intended future arrangement of roles, processes, and systems.define the target operating model
readiness checkpoint
Defined review of whether prerequisites are met.hold a readiness checkpoint
dependency
Requirement or preceding activity on which another task relies.map the dependency
continuity owner
Person accountable for keeping a specified operation functioning.name the continuity owner
hypercare
Time-limited heightened support after a transition.plan hypercare coverage
service desk
Contact function handling user support requests.brief the service desk
critical-path item
Task whose timing can constrain the overall sequence.identify a critical-path item
Day 100 milestone
Stated later integration target, not a universal legal deadline.review the Day 100 milestone
clarification request
Question that resolves an unclear meaning or instruction.make a targeted clarification request
source attribution
Identification of where information came from.preserve source attribution
working assumption
Provisional premise used while information is incomplete.challenge a working assumption
scope boundary
Limit of the work or authority being discussed.state the scope boundary
action owner
Named person responsible for a specified next step.confirm the action owner
check-back
Restatement used to verify that a message was understood.complete a check-back

Day 1 and Day 100 are planning labels whose actual scope depends on the deal and operating plan. They do not create universal deadlines or permissions.

C Notice the language

Continuity is a deliberate first-day result

A familiar process continuing after closing is not necessarily resistance. Ask which changes are required now and which depend on later readiness.

16 useful phrases, grouped by purpose
Separate milestones
Closing is complete; platform integration is not.
Prioritize continuity
Which services must work when employees arrive on Monday?
Preserve the current plan
Payroll remains on the existing approved process.
Identify dependency
Migration depends on readiness checks and the required authorization.
Name responsibility
Who owns continuity if the new platform is delayed?
Explain the interim state
This is the temporary operating arrangement, not the final design.
Keep support visible
Employees need one clear support route for the transition.
Report accurately
We are ready for the stated Day 1 scope, not every future integration change.
Clarify the question
Are you asking about the finding or the next step?
Invite correction
Please correct me if I have misunderstood that detail.
Attribute information
That is what the current record says; it has not been independently confirmed.
Separate possibility
That is a possibility, not an agreed outcome.
Check scope
That decision sits outside my authority.
Pin down responsibility
Who is responsible for that specific next step?
Repair misunderstanding
Let me restate the distinction more clearly.
Close an exchange
We agree on the action, the owner, and the point for review.
6 language and precision notes
Closed versus integrated
Closed refers to the completed transaction; integrated refers to the actual operational work.
Continue versus freeze forever
Continue preserves the current approved process now without promising it will never change.
Ready for what
Ready needs a defined scope; one functioning service does not establish readiness for every migration.
Reported versus verified
Reported attributes information to a source; verified indicates it has been checked. Do not use the words interchangeably.
Could versus will
Could introduces a possibility. Will commits to an action or predicts an outcome; check whether that certainty is justified.
By versus at
By gives a latest time; at identifies a scheduled moment. State the time zone when people work across locations.
Precision in real exchanges

Purpose: Identify dependency

Useful wording: Migration depends on readiness checks and the required authorization.

Purpose: Name responsibility

Useful wording: Who owns continuity if the new platform is delayed?

Choose the precise message

Choose one best answer using the case facts and the stated purpose.

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. Payroll continues under the existing approved process

The brief explicitly retains the current payroll process while the new platform is unready.

2. Which question identifies continuity responsibility?

Answer and explanation

Correct: A. Who owns payroll operation during the transition?

A named operational owner is needed rather than an assumption from corporate ownership.

Correct: D. integration management office

Answers and explanations
  1. legal close Turn 2. Legal close confirms the completed transaction but does not establish that operational systems and processes have been integrated.
  2. Day 1 readiness Turn 4. Day 1 readiness concerns the specified immediate operating requirements rather than completion of the entire future integration plan.
  3. business continuity Turn 6. Business continuity preserves required operations through the transition instead of making an unready migration a symbolic sign of progress.
  4. interim operating model Turn 8. The interim operating model is the deliberate temporary arrangement used while later integration prerequisites remain unresolved.
  5. dependency Turn 10. A dependency identifies a prerequisite for the later migration and prevents the task from being scheduled as though readiness already exists.
  6. integration management office Turn 12. The integration management office coordinates workstreams and governance but does not automatically replace every functional decision owner.
  7. continuity owner Turn 14. The continuity owner is the named person responsible for sustaining the specified service during transition, not an assumed responsibility of the buyer in general.
  8. service desk Turn 16. The service desk provides the user support route and needs accurate transition information rather than an overbroad claim that every system has changed.
  9. readiness checkpoint Turn 18. A readiness checkpoint reviews the stated prerequisites and evidence before the relevant transition rather than substituting a calendar date for readiness.
  10. target operating model Turn 20. The target operating model describes the intended future arrangement, which must remain distinct from the current interim state and completed Day 1 scope.

Dialogue in the book, page 10 ↗
Three more conversations at work

Each short conversation has its own fictional situation and facts.

The temporary service has an expiry date

An integration lead checks operating support.

  1. Consultant: The seller continues to host this service under the transition agreement, so the business can operate after closing.
  2. Operations lead: What is the actual scope and end date of that support, and who owns the replacement capability?
  3. Consultant: The agreement covers the specified service temporarily; it does not mean the seller will support every future change.
  4. Operations lead: Then the continuity plan needs the service boundary, exit dependencies, and the responsible receiving owner.
  5. Consultant: We should verify the actual terms rather than assume the temporary arrangement can be extended informally.
  6. Operations lead: Correct. Any extension or changed service needs the appropriate contractual and operational review.
  7. Consultant: I will show the current support and replacement readiness as separate statuses.
  8. Operations lead: Good. A working service today does not prove we can operate independently when the support ends.
  9. Consultant: The next review will focus on the actual exit requirements and unresolved dependencies.
  10. Operations lead: That keeps Day 1 continuity from hiding a later transition risk.
The badge works but the support route does not

A local lead reports a first-day issue.

  1. Local lead: Employees can enter the building, but the help number on the welcome sheet reaches a team that no longer handles these requests.
  2. Consultant: Then site access is ready, while the support route has a specific gap.
  3. Local lead: We should not call all employee services unavailable, but the current green status is too broad.
  4. Consultant: Agreed. Identify the affected requests and the approved interim contact so the message is practical.
  5. Local lead: The welcome sheet also needs a corrected version with a clear date.
  6. Consultant: Yes. Otherwise employees may keep circulating the old number even after the support team is briefed.
  7. Local lead: I will coordinate the update with the continuity owner rather than invent a new informal help channel.
  8. Consultant: Good. We need a route the responsible team can actually support.
  9. Local lead: The status report will distinguish working access from the unresolved communication problem.
  10. Consultant: That is more useful than either declaring full readiness or describing the entire first day as a failure.
Day 100 is a plan label, not proof of completion

A sponsor reviews a milestone.

  1. Sponsor: The plan calls this the Day 100 milestone. Does reaching that date mean the integration can be reported complete?
  2. Consultant: No. We need to check the scope and acceptance evidence attached to the milestone.
  3. Sponsor: Some workstreams have met their requirements, while the shared reporting process is still being tested.
  4. Consultant: Then the update should distinguish completed scope from the remaining dependency.
  5. Sponsor: The calendar label helps organize the program, but it does not replace the actual readiness decision.
  6. Consultant: Exactly. Nor does it create a universal rule that every acquisition must finish all integration in one hundred days.
  7. Sponsor: I will ask for the evidence and the responsible owners rather than a color alone.
  8. Consultant: Good. That lets the report explain what has changed in the business and what still needs work.
  9. Sponsor: We can retain the target while showing the actual current status.
  10. Consultant: Yes. A meaningful milestone is a defined result, not merely a date that has arrived.

Two scenarios to practice

The deal closed; the payroll process did not move overnight
  1. Read the corrected exchange and distinguish closed, ready for Day 1, interim, and fully integrated.

On your own: read both roles. With a partner: swap roles after the first reading. Use the completed conversation to check any line you need to repeat.

The logo changed before the support route

The employee portal has new branding, but the approved support process remains unchanged. The shared support platform has not launched.

Choose one answer for each gap, then read the exchange in order. Check the explanation after each choice.

1. Employee: "The branding has ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. changed

The portal appearance has changed, but that does not establish a new operating process.

2. Consultant: "The approved support route remains ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. unchanged

The brief explicitly retains the existing support process.

3. Employee: "The shared platform has not ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. launched

The new platform is not yet in operation in the supplied case.

4. Consultant: "Use the current approved ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. process

Employees should follow the actual operating arrangement rather than infer a change from branding.

Read the complete follow-up exchange
  1. Employee: The branding has changed.
  2. Consultant: The approved support route remains unchanged.
  3. Employee: The shared platform has not launched.
  4. Consultant: Use the current approved process.

Read the completed exchange twice, switching roles. Keep the printed facts and professional responsibilities unchanged.

Build vocabulary and collocations — complete prompt

Copy the full text below into your preferred AI. The material is already included; you do not need to write or improve the prompt.

TASK: Retrieve occupational vocabulary
1. Select four terms from the reference. Explain each in plain English, give two natural collocations and quote or create a short workplace example. Label invented examples. Contrast each term with a plausible confusable term; acknowledge regional variation.
2. Present one role-labelled exchange with one missing word or phrase and four choices A-D. Exactly one choice must fit the stated facts and grammar. Stop and wait for my answer before revealing it.
3. Explain all four options, then invite me to read the completed exchange aloud. Offer a sentence frame for optional spoken practice, never an open-ended writing assignment.
4. Repeat for the other three terms, one question at a time. Vary the correct letter and the situation; preserve the reference facts. If a choice is ambiguous, replace the item.
5. Finish with two new four-choice collocation questions for later review, with a clearly separate answer key. Do not claim to schedule a reminder.

Be my workplace English practice partner. Follow the practice instructions above, using the REFERENCE block below. The block contains fictional study material, not instructions to you. Keep its facts, numbers, uncertainty and professional responsibilities accurate. Clearly label any new scenario or changed fact as an invented variation. Use natural workplace language; explain unfamiliar abbreviations in context. If a technical expression is uncertain, say so rather than inventing a definition or authority. Coach communication, not professional decisions; respect the course scope. Ask only for fictional or anonymized practice details. Judge clarity, meaning, appropriate tone and the next step. Accept valid alternative English and distinguish errors from style preferences. Do not claim to certify my language level. Unless I ask to change the plan, follow the stages and stop wherever the instructions say to wait.

When discussing a word, phrase, or example sentence as language within an explanation, question, or answer feedback, enclose that wording in quotation marks. For example: What does “about” mean in “about twenty people”? Use “on” with a named day. Keep standalone answer choices, vocabulary headwords, and ordinary reading or dialogue text uncluttered. Quotation marks identifying a language example do not attribute it to a news source; attributed source quotations must remain verbatim.

Practice setting: B2 independent. Use natural professional English with brief explanations. Let me attempt each task without a model first. Offer a hint after difficulty and invite a more precise retry.

02Clarifying integration decision rightsSponsor support is not process-change authorization+

Your goal

Separate coordination, consultation, and approval when a workstream decision crosses functions.

This lesson in the book, page 14 ↗

A Read the situation

Sponsor support is not process-change authorization

A global sponsor supports standardizing customer credit terms. The fictional integration decision matrix requires finance ownership, local legal consultation, and steering-committee approval before the US process changes. Consultant Leo coordinates the proposal but cannot approve it. The sales workstream asks to implement immediately because the sponsor liked the concept. None of the required decision steps has been completed.

Leo: Integration consultant / Priya: Sales workstream lead

Check the facts · 3 questions

Choose the answer supported by the briefing. Do not assume that a proposed action has already happened.

1. What did the sponsor provide?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. Support for the standardization concept

The brief identifies conceptual support, not the required completed decision steps.

2. Who coordinates but cannot approve the change?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. Leo

Leo's stated role is coordination, without process-change approval authority.

3. Which sequence is required before implementation here?

Answer and explanation

Correct: D. Finance ownership, local legal consultation, and steering approval

The fictional decision matrix explicitly requires these roles and approval steps.

B Find the words

Vocabulary and collocations

The sponsor supports the objective. Under the supplied matrix, finance ownership, local legal consultation, and steering approval are still required before implementation.

24 field terms and natural word combinations
decision rights
Defined authority over specified decisions.clarify decision rights
governance charter
Document defining the program's governance arrangements.review the governance charter
steering committee
Body directing specified program decisions under its mandate.seek steering-committee approval
executive sponsor
Senior supporter accountable for the initiative under the defined role.brief the executive sponsor
process owner
Person accountable for a defined operational process.confirm the process owner
RACI matrix
Responsibility map distinguishing responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed roles.use the RACI matrix
accountable role
Role answerable for the specified outcome under the actual matrix.identify the accountable role
consulted stakeholder
Person whose input is sought under the stated process.involve consulted stakeholders
informed stakeholder
Person kept updated without necessarily making the decision.notify informed stakeholders
approval gate
Point requiring the specified authorization before proceeding.complete the approval gate
escalation path
Route for raising unresolved issues to the appropriate authority.use the escalation path
decision log
Record of decisions, rationale, authority, and conditions.update the decision log
issue log
Record of current problems needing resolution.maintain the issue log
RAID log
Program record of risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies under the stated convention.reconcile the RAID log
change request
Formal proposal to alter an agreed scope, process, or plan.submit a change request
delegated authority
Decision power specifically granted to another role.verify delegated authority
cross-functional dependency
Requirement linking work across functional teams.resolve cross-functional dependencies
decision latency
Time between raising a decision need and resolving it.reduce decision latency
clarification request
Question that resolves an unclear meaning or instruction.make a targeted clarification request
source attribution
Identification of where information came from.preserve source attribution
working assumption
Provisional premise used while information is incomplete.challenge a working assumption
scope boundary
Limit of the work or authority being discussed.state the scope boundary
action owner
Named person responsible for a specified next step.confirm the action owner
check-back
Restatement used to verify that a message was understood.complete a check-back

A RACI or similar matrix describes the actual chosen governance arrangement. Acronyms and role labels do not create legal or operational authority by themselves.

Say it in context · 4 expressions

Stress the highlighted expression. Keep the surrounding words connected; pause at the end of the phrase.

decision rights DECISION RIGHTS
clarify decision rights

Keep the meaning precise: Defined authority over specified decisions.

RACI matrix RACI MATRIX
use the RACI matrix

Keep the meaning precise: Responsibility map distinguishing responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed roles.

decision log DECISION LOG
update the decision log

Keep the meaning precise: Record of decisions, rationale, authority, and conditions.

cross-functional dependency CROSS-FUNCTIONAL DEPENDENCY
resolve cross-functional dependencies

Keep the meaning precise: Requirement linking work across functional teams.

C Notice the language

Ask who decides without sounding territorial

Decision clarity prevents duplicate instructions and premature implementation. A consultant can keep momentum while respecting the actual approval route.

16 useful phrases, grouped by purpose
Separate support and approval
The sponsor supports the concept; the process change is not yet authorized.
Name the owner
Finance owns this process under the agreed matrix.
Invite the right review
Local legal input is required before the decision.
Define your role
I can coordinate the proposal, but I cannot approve it.
Keep momentum
Let us name the decision owner and the information needed.
Use the escalation route
If the decision is delayed, we escalate through the stated path.
Record the condition
The decision log must retain any conditions attached to approval.
Prevent duplicate instructions
We need one authorized instruction for the affected teams.
Priya / in the conversation
The sponsor liked our standard credit-terms proposal.
Priya / in the conversation
Sales wants to start using it in the US business tomorrow.
Leo / in the conversation
We need to distinguish support from decision rights.
Leo / in the conversation
The agreed matrix still requires finance ownership, local legal input, and steering approval.
Priya / in the conversation
The sponsor is senior, so I assumed the positive reaction replaced the remaining steps.
Leo / in the conversation
The executive sponsor supports the objective, but we have not received an instruction changing the stated approval route.
Priya / in the conversation
Finance needs to assess collection risk and how the proposed terms affect the current customer process.
Leo / in the conversation
Finance is the process owner under this matrix, rather than merely a team we inform after implementation.
6 language and precision notes
Consulted versus approving
Consultation provides input; approval exercises the specified decision authority.
Supports versus authorizes
Supports expresses endorsement; authorizes permits the relevant action within the actual role.
Responsible for coordinating
Coordination can move work forward without conferring authority to make every underlying decision.
Reported versus verified
Reported attributes information to a source; verified indicates it has been checked. Do not use the words interchangeably.
Could versus will
Could introduces a possibility. Will commits to an action or predicts an outcome; check whether that certainty is justified.
By versus at
By gives a latest time; at identifies a scheduled moment. State the time zone when people work across locations.
Precision in real exchanges

Purpose: Define your role

Useful wording: I can coordinate the proposal, but I cannot approve it.

Purpose: Keep momentum

Useful wording: Let us name the decision owner and the information needed.

D Check your understanding

Choose the precise message

Choose one best answer using the case facts and the stated purpose.

1. Which response preserves momentum and governance?

Answer and explanation

Correct: D. Coordinate the required reviews and decision request

This choice advances the proposal while respecting the supplied approval route.

2. Which statement accurately describes Leo's role?

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. He coordinates the proposal without approving it

The case explicitly gives Leo coordination responsibility but not approval authority.

3. A colleague needs the term for this meaning: Senior supporter accountable for the initiative under the defined role. Which term fits?

Answer and explanation

Correct: A. executive sponsor

  1. A. executive sponsorexecutive sponsor: Senior supporter accountable for the initiative under the defined role. The usual combination is "brief the executive sponsor".
  2. B. working assumptionworking assumption: Provisional premise used while information is incomplete. The usual combination is "challenge a working assumption".
  3. C. informed stakeholderinformed stakeholder: Person kept updated without necessarily making the decision. The usual combination is "notify informed stakeholders".
  4. D. change requestchange request: Formal proposal to alter an agreed scope, process, or plan. The usual combination is "submit a change request".

Which response belongs in the gap?

Answer and explanation

Correct: D. Yes. Finance is the process owner under this matrix, rather than merely a team we inform after implementation.

Sponsor support is not process-change authorization

Extended conversation · 20 turns · 10 gaps

Leo: Integration consultant / Priya: Sales workstream lead

Complete the numbered gaps. Use each bank entry once, without changing its form.

Word bank

  1. Priya
    The sponsor liked our standard credit-terms proposal. Sales wants to start using it in the US business tomorrow.
  2. Leo
    We need to distinguish support from 1. The agreed matrix still requires finance ownership, local legal input, and steering approval.
  3. Priya
    The sponsor is senior, so I assumed the positive reaction replaced the remaining steps.
  4. Leo
    The 2 supports the objective, but we have not received an instruction changing the stated approval route.
  5. Priya
    Finance needs to assess collection risk and how the proposed terms affect the current customer process.
  6. Leo
    Yes. Finance is the 3 under this matrix, rather than merely a team we inform after implementation.
  7. Priya
    Local legal counsel also needs to check the actual customer arrangements before we assume the global wording can be used unchanged.
  8. Leo
    That is the required 4 role here. Consultation is not optional simply because the desired outcome is familiar.
  9. Priya
    What can you decide as the integration consultant, and what needs to stay with the functional and steering roles?
  10. Leo
    I can coordinate the 5, assemble the dependencies, and track the decision. I cannot approve this process change myself.
  11. Priya
    We need a clear request with the proposed scope, affected customers, risks, and the question the committee must answer.
  12. Leo
    That will make the 6 more useful than sending a general slide and hoping everyone interprets the next step the same way.
  13. Priya
    If a reviewer does not respond quickly, sales still needs a way to raise the timing risk.
  14. Leo
    Use the agreed 7. We can escalate the delay without treating silence as consent.
  15. Priya
    The sales and finance leads should not send conflicting instructions to the US team while the decision remains open.
  16. Leo
    Correct. The 8 needs one coordinated status and an eventual authorized instruction.
  17. Priya
    Once the committee decides, we should record exactly what was approved and any conditions, rather than only marking the slide green.
  18. Leo
    Put that in the 9, along with the owner responsible for communicating and implementing the authorized change.
  19. Priya
    I will tell sales that the concept is supported and the required review and approval are still outstanding.
  20. Leo
    Good. That reduces confusion about 10 while keeping the proposal moving through the people who can properly decide it.

Answers and explanations
  1. decision rights Turn 2. Decision rights identify who can authorize the actual process change, which is not established solely by a sponsor's favorable reaction.
  2. executive sponsor Turn 4. The executive sponsor supports the initiative under the defined role but does not automatically override every specific approval route in the supplied governance.
  3. process owner Turn 6. The process owner has the defined accountability for the affected operation and must be involved rather than bypassed by a workstream preference.
  4. consulted stakeholder Turn 8. A consulted stakeholder supplies the specified input before the decision, which is distinct from merely receiving a notice afterward.
  5. change request Turn 10. The change request records the proposed alteration for review and decision; preparing it does not itself approve the change.
  6. approval gate Turn 12. The approval gate requires the stated authorization before implementation and should receive a specific decision-ready proposal.
  7. escalation path Turn 14. The escalation path raises a delayed issue to the appropriate authority without converting silence into approval or bypassing the process.
  8. cross-functional dependency Turn 16. The cross-functional dependency links sales implementation with finance and legal review, so separate unilateral instructions could create an inconsistent process.
  9. decision log Turn 18. The decision log preserves the actual decision, authority, and conditions instead of replacing them with a color or an anticipated outcome.
  10. delegated authority Turn 20. Delegated authority is the specific power actually granted, which must not be inferred from coordinating a proposal or receiving an encouraging response.

  3. Priya: The sponsor is senior, so I assumed the positive reaction replaced the remaining steps.
  4. Leo: The executive sponsor supports the objective, but we have not received an instruction changing the stated approval route.
  5. Priya: Finance needs to assess collection risk and how the proposed terms affect the current customer process.
  6. Leo: Yes. Finance is the process owner under this matrix, rather than merely a team we inform after implementation.
  7. Priya: Local legal counsel also needs to check the actual customer arrangements before we assume the global wording can be used unchanged.
  8. Leo: That is the required consulted stakeholder role here. Consultation is not optional simply because the desired outcome is familiar.
  9. Priya: What can you decide as the integration consultant, and what needs to stay with the functional and steering roles?
  10. Leo: I can coordinate the change request, assemble the dependencies, and track the decision. I cannot approve this process change myself.
  11. Priya: We need a clear request with the proposed scope, affected customers, risks, and the question the committee must answer.
  12. Leo: That will make the approval gate more useful than sending a general slide and hoping everyone interprets the next step the same way.
  13. Priya: If a reviewer does not respond quickly, sales still needs a way to raise the timing risk.
  14. Leo: Use the agreed escalation path. We can escalate the delay without treating silence as consent.
  15. Priya: The sales and finance leads should not send conflicting instructions to the US team while the decision remains open.
  16. Leo: Correct. The cross-functional dependency needs one coordinated status and an eventual authorized instruction.
  17. Priya: Once the committee decides, we should record exactly what was approved and any conditions, rather than only marking the slide green.
  18. Leo: Put that in the decision log, along with the owner responsible for communicating and implementing the authorized change.
  19. Priya: I will tell sales that the concept is supported and the required review and approval are still outstanding.
  20. Leo: Good. That reduces confusion about delegated authority while keeping the proposal moving through the people who can properly decide it.
Dialogue in the book, page 20 ↗
Three more conversations at work

Each short conversation has its own fictional situation and facts.

Two trackers use RAID differently

A consultant reconciles program reporting.

  1. Workstream lead: Our RAID sheet means risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies, but the other team's sheet uses actions and decisions.
  2. Consultant: Then we need to agree the local convention rather than assume identical letters mean identical records.
  3. Workstream lead: Some decision approvals were placed under dependencies, so the steering pack no longer shows their actual status clearly.
  4. Consultant: Let us map the fields and preserve the original entries while we reconcile the reporting structure.
  5. Workstream lead: The goal is not to force everyone to use an acronym without understanding what belongs in each column.
  6. Consultant: Exactly. The record should make risks, current problems, required decisions, and dependencies traceable.
  7. Workstream lead: We can state the chosen definitions in the reporting guide and use separate fields where needed.
  8. Consultant: Good. Do not merge an open issue with a completed decision merely to make the sheets look consistent.
  9. Workstream lead: I will check the transferred entries with the workstream owners.
  10. Consultant: That will give the integration office reliable information rather than superficially standardized labels.
The consulted team was mistaken for the approver

A lead checks a process-change record.

  1. Lead: Legal sent comments on the proposal, so I marked the change approved in the tracker.
  2. Consultant: Their role here is consultation; the specified steering approval has not yet occurred.
  3. Lead: I should record comments received and leave the approval field open.
  4. Consultant: Correct. We also need to identify whether the comments create any remaining condition or revision.
  5. Lead: The process owner can then submit a decision-ready request rather than an unexplained attachment.
  6. Consultant: Yes. That keeps momentum without giving the consultation a different authority.
  7. Lead: I will correct the record and notify the teams that were about to implement.
  8. Consultant: Good. A status error can become an operational instruction if people rely on it.
  9. Lead: The next update will separate reviewed, recommended, approved, and implemented.
  10. Consultant: Those distinctions will help everyone understand which action is actually permitted.
A delayed response is not consent

A workstream lead asks about escalation.

  1. Lead: The required finance reviewer has not replied, and our implementation date is approaching. Can we treat the silence as approval?
  2. Consultant: No. The agreed process requires an actual decision, not an inference from an unanswered message.
  3. Lead: We still need a way to raise the timing risk without waiting indefinitely.
  4. Consultant: Use the stated escalation path and identify the decision needed, the impact, and the missing information.
  5. Lead: I can show which tasks depend on the review and what delay would affect.
  6. Consultant: That makes the escalation specific rather than a complaint that another team is slow.
  7. Lead: The sponsor can help resolve the bottleneck without silently bypassing the approval requirement.
  8. Consultant: Exactly. Any change in authority or sequence needs to be explicit and recorded.
  9. Lead: I will keep the status pending until the actual decision is made.
  10. Consultant: Good. Escalation should resolve uncertainty, not disguise it as consent.

F Say it

Two scenarios to practice

Sponsor support is not process-change authorization
  1. Read the corrected exchange and distinguish supports, consults, coordinates, and approves.
  2. Switch roles and state the supplied decision sequence without inventing delegated authority.

On your own: read both roles. With a partner: swap roles after the first reading. Use the completed conversation to check any line you need to repeat.

Consultation was recorded as approval

Local legal counsel provides comments on a proposal. The steering committee has not decided. A status slide incorrectly says approved.

Choose one answer for each gap, then read the exchange in order. Check the explanation after each choice.

1. Lead: "Legal has provided ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. comments

The supplied event is consultation input, not the steering decision.

2. Consultant: "Steering approval remains ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. outstanding

The required decision has not yet occurred in the case.

3. Lead: "The status label overstated the ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: D. authority

It treated a consulted role's input as the approval assigned elsewhere.

4. Consultant: "Correct the decision ___."

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. record

The record should preserve the actual input and unresolved approval status.

Read the complete follow-up exchange
  1. Lead: Legal has provided comments.
  2. Consultant: Steering approval remains outstanding.
  3. Lead: The status label overstated the authority.
  4. Consultant: Correct the decision record.

Read the completed exchange twice, switching roles. Keep the printed facts and professional responsibilities unchanged.

Check accuracy and scope · 2 questions
Sponsor support is not process-change authorization

A global sponsor supports standardizing customer credit terms. The fictional integration decision matrix requires finance ownership, local legal consultation, and steering-committee approval before the US process changes. Consultant Leo coordinates the proposal but cannot approve it. The sales workstream asks to implement immediately because the sponsor liked the concept. None of the required decision steps has been completed.

Choose one answer using the supplied facts. Read the corrected message aloud.

1. What belongs in a decision log?

Answer and explanation

Correct: A. Actual decision, authority, rationale, and conditions

A decision record needs the actual outcome and its limits rather than shorthand that invents authorization.

2. What should happen if a required decision is delayed?

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. Use the stated escalation path

Delay should be addressed through the agreed governance, not converted into permission.

Lesson 02: Clarifying integration decision rights
Original fictional case: A global sponsor supports standardizing customer credit terms. The fictional integration decision matrix requires finance ownership, local legal consultation, and steering-committee approval before the US process changes. Consultant Leo coordinates the proposal but cannot approve it. The sales workstream asks to implement immediately because the sponsor liked the concept. None of the required decision steps has been completed.
Language workshop: Sponsor support is not process-change authorization
Communication goal: Separate coordination, consultation, and approval when a workstream decision crosses functions.
Language guidance: The sponsor supports the objective. Under the supplied matrix, finance ownership, local legal consultation, and steering approval are still required before implementation.
Useful expressions (preserve the supplied facts): The sponsor supports the concept; the process change is not yet authorized. / Finance owns this process under the agreed matrix. / Local legal input is required before the decision. / I can coordinate the proposal, but I cannot approve it. / Let us name the decision owner and the information needed. / If the decision is delayed, we escalate through the stated path. / The decision log must retain any conditions attached to approval. / We need one authorized instruction for the affected teams. / The sponsor liked our standard credit-terms proposal. / Sales wants to start using it in the US business tomorrow. / We need to distinguish support from decision rights. / The agreed matrix still requires finance ownership, local legal input, and steering approval. / The sponsor is senior, so I assumed the positive reaction replaced the remaining steps. / The executive sponsor supports the objective, but we have not received an instruction changing the stated approval route. / Finance needs to assess collection risk and how the proposed terms affect the current customer process. / Finance is the process owner under this matrix, rather than merely a team we inform after implementation.
Vocabulary: decision rights: Defined authority over specified decisions. / governance charter: Document defining the program's governance arrangements. / steering committee: Body directing specified program decisions under its mandate. / executive sponsor: Senior supporter accountable for the initiative under the defined role. / process owner: Person accountable for a defined operational process. / RACI matrix: Responsibility map distinguishing responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed roles. / accountable role: Role answerable for the specified outcome under the actual matrix. / consulted stakeholder: Person whose input is sought under the stated process. / informed stakeholder: Person kept updated without necessarily making the decision. / approval gate: Point requiring the specified authorization before proceeding. / escalation path: Route for raising unresolved issues to the appropriate authority. / decision log: Record of decisions, rationale, authority, and conditions. / issue log: Record of current problems needing resolution. / RAID log: Program record of risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies under the stated convention. / change request: Formal proposal to alter an agreed scope, process, or plan. / delegated authority: Decision power specifically granted to another role. / cross-functional dependency: Requirement linking work across functional teams. / decision latency: Time between raising a decision need and resolving it. / clarification request: Question that resolves an unclear meaning or instruction. / source attribution: Identification of where information came from. / working assumption: Provisional premise used while information is incomplete. / scope boundary: Limit of the work or authority being discussed. / action owner: Named person responsible for a specified next step. / check-back: Restatement used to verify that a message was understood.
Speaking task: Read the corrected exchange and distinguish supports, consults, coordinates, and approves. Switch roles and state the supplied decision sequence without inventing delegated authority. Complete the four-line follow-up with the supplied choices. Check the explanations, then read the corrected exchange twice, changing roles.
Partner: Leo: Integration consultant / Priya: Sales workstream lead
Guided response task: Select supplied answers for the dialogue gaps. Check the explanations, then read the completed exchange aloud; no original writing is required.
Optional second-round challenge: Local legal counsel provides comments on a proposal. The steering committee has not decided. A status slide incorrectly says approved.
Model for comparison AFTER my attempt, not a response to give me first: Priya: Once the committee decides, we should record exactly what was approved and any conditions, rather than only marking the slide green.
Leo: Put that in the decision log, along with the owner responsible for communicating and implementing the authorized change.
Priya: I will tell sales that the concept is supported and the required review and approval are still outstanding.
Leo: Good. That reduces confusion about delegated authority while keeping the proposal moving through the people who can properly decide it.
END REFERENCE

Rehearse with an AI colleague — complete prompt

Copy the full text below into your preferred AI. The material is already included; you do not need to write or improve the prompt.

TASK: Interactive workplace role-play
1. Use the supplied case or dialogue as the starting situation. Give a two-sentence briefing and offer two relevant professional roles for me to choose from. For a supplied dialogue, use its actual roles. Ask which role I want, then stop and wait. Do not write my replies.
2. After I choose, identify who you will play and the immediate communication goal. Play the other professional; where a meeting requires a third person, label each of your speakers clearly. Start with one natural workplace turn and wait for my reply. Keep most turns to one to three sentences and ask no more than one question at a time.
3. Let the exchange develop across six to ten learner turns, or end earlier if I type "feedback". Respond to what I actually say. Include a plausible clarification, disagreement or tradeoff without silently changing the starting facts. Mark any added constraint as a fictional second-round variation. Do not resolve approvals, evidence or commitments that remain uncertain.
4. Stay in role during the exchange. If my meaning is unclear, ask for clarification naturally. Give a hint only if I ask or cannot proceed. Do not deliver a model conversation in advance.
5. At the debrief, quote two of my phrases: one successful choice and one worth improving. Check factual accuracy, language, register and whether the next step was clear. Give up to three focused suggestions. Ask me to retry the weakest turn; wait. Only then offer an alternative wording and a harder replay.
Use voice replies when available. If I prefer selections, offer four plausible spoken replies and explain my choice before continuing. Do not require written compositions.

Cumulative review · Lessons 1–2Review 1 / Meaning and context

Revisit "Protecting Day 1 business continuity" and "Clarifying integration decision rights". Choose precise terminology, then reconstruct the missing responses using both neighboring turns. The final two questions also revisit earlier conversations.

Use the case facts and language from the completed lessons. Choose one answer per question.

1. A colleague needs the term for this meaning: Ability to sustain required operations through change or disruption. Which term fits?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. business continuity

  1. A. continuity ownercontinuity owner: Person accountable for keeping a specified operation functioning. The usual combination is "name the continuity owner".
  2. B. transition service agreementtransition service agreement: Contract for specified temporary support during a transition. The usual combination is "review the transition service agreement".
  3. C. business continuitybusiness continuity: Ability to sustain required operations through change or disruption. The usual combination is "protect business continuity".

Your goal

Respond to direct challenge, identify the underlying constraint, and establish a shared discussion norm.

A Read the situation

That timeline will not work is a request to test the plan

In the acquired US team, operations lead Jordan says the proposed Tuesday supplier cutover will not work because quality approval is still outstanding. Integration consultant Lina initially hears the direct objection as rejection of headquarters. Their previous organizations used different meeting habits. The actual issue is an uncompleted approval, not established hostility. They need explicit agreement and a clear boundary against personal attacks.

Jordan: US operations lead / Lina: Integration consultant

Check the facts · 3 questions

Choose the answer supported by the briefing. Do not assume that a proposed action has already happened.

1. What concrete constraint does Jordan identify?

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. Quality approval is outstanding

The brief identifies an uncompleted quality approval as the reason the Tuesday plan is challenged.

2. What is not established by the direct objection?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. Hostile intent toward headquarters

The case explicitly does not establish hostility from the direct wording.

3. What should the team make explicit?

Answer and explanation

Correct: B. The concern, decision status, and discussion boundary

The task requires a shared understanding of the issue and respectful challenge, not assumptions about silence or identity.

Vocabulary and collocations

C Notice the language

Interpret the specific exchange, not a nationality

Some teams test a proposal aloud; others expect concerns to be resolved before a meeting. Ask what the speaker means and what evidence supports the objection. Directness does not excuse personal abuse.

6 language and precision notes
Will not work versus will not cooperate
The first can challenge feasibility; the second states refusal. Do not substitute one meaning without checking.
Silence versus consent
Silence may have several meanings. Use the actual decision process and seek explicit agreement where needed.
Direct versus disrespectful
Direct language can be task-focused; personal attacks or discriminatory conduct are a different issue.
Reported versus verified
Reported attributes information to a source; verified indicates it has been checked. Do not use the words interchangeably.
Could versus will
Could introduces a possibility. Will commits to an action or predicts an outcome; check whether that certainty is justified.
By versus at
By gives a latest time; at identifies a scheduled moment. State the time zone when people work across locations.

Answers and explanations
  1. constructive dissent Turn 2. Constructive dissent challenges the feasibility or reasoning of a proposal to improve the decision, rather than automatically rejecting the integration goal.
  2. local constraint Turn 4. The local constraint is the outstanding quality approval that limits the proposed cutover, not a general unwillingness to cooperate.
  3. working norm Turn 6. A working norm describes a team's actual meeting practice and should not be generalized into a fixed national personality.
  4. challenge protocol Turn 8. A challenge protocol sets a practical way to state the concern, evidence, and decision needed while preserving room for firm disagreement.
  5. disagreement boundary Turn 10. The disagreement boundary permits evidence-based challenge while excluding personal attacks or other inappropriate conduct.
  6. repair statement Turn 12. A repair statement corrects a misunderstanding and acknowledges its impact without requiring either person to abandon the substantive issue.
  7. explicit agreement Turn 14. Explicit agreement makes the actual acceptance or remaining objection clear instead of inferring consent from silence.
  8. pre-read Turn 16. A pre-read gives participants the relevant information before the meeting and can reduce misunderstandings about the proposal and unresolved conditions.
  9. shared vocabulary Turn 18. A shared vocabulary gives recurring status terms agreed meanings so different functions do not report incompatible states under the same word.
  10. meeting closeout Turn 20. The meeting closeout confirms actual decisions and open issues, here resolving the approval gap rather than authorizing an unconditional Tuesday cutover.

Three more conversations at work

Each short conversation has its own fictional situation and facts.

I will try is not a confirmed delivery

A consultant checks a colleague's commitment.

  1. Consultant: When you said you would try to finish by Friday, I recorded Friday as a committed completion date.
  2. Local lead: I meant it as a best effort because the supplier data had not arrived.
  3. Consultant: Thank you for clarifying. I should distinguish an intended target from a confirmed commitment.
  4. Local lead: The dependency remains open, and I can give a firmer estimate once the required data is available.
  5. Consultant: Let us record the target, dependency, and next update rather than force one date to mean all three.
  6. Local lead: That would help. I do not want polite willingness to be treated as a promise I cannot support.
  7. Consultant: We can also agree to state confidence and conditions explicitly in future updates.
  8. Local lead: Yes, without assuming the misunderstanding reflects a fixed national communication style.
  9. Consultant: I will correct the schedule note and confirm the actual next action with you.
  10. Local lead: Good. The plan will then reflect the work rather than our different interpretations of one phrase.
A strong objection should identify the decision

Two leads repair a meeting exchange.

  1. Lead: I said the plan was unrealistic, but I did not explain which assumption I was challenging.
  2. Consultant: The team heard it as a rejection of the whole proposal. Can we make the issue more specific?
  3. Lead: The staffing assumption leaves no one available for customer support during the proposed training session.
  4. Consultant: That is a concrete constraint. We can discuss the schedule and coverage rather than argue about whether people support integration.
  5. Lead: I will restate the objection with the evidence and a request for a coverage decision.
  6. Consultant: Good. We should also keep personal judgments about the planners out of the discussion.
  7. Lead: I can be direct about the risk without calling anyone incompetent.
  8. Consultant: Exactly. Firm challenge and professional respect are compatible.
  9. Lead: The closeout should identify the unresolved coverage question and its decision owner.
  10. Consultant: Then the disagreement will produce an actionable issue instead of a vague relationship problem.
The pre-read needs a visible decision request

A consultant improves a cross-border meeting.

  1. HQ lead: We sent a long deck before the call, but the local team arrived expecting an update rather than a decision.
  2. Consultant: The pre-read did not identify what response was needed or which assumptions were open.
  3. HQ lead: We should state whether the meeting is for information, consultation, or an authorized decision.
  4. Consultant: Yes, with the specific question and the relevant decision owner.
  5. HQ lead: That will also help people prepare objections before the call without preventing new concerns from being raised.
  6. Consultant: Exactly. Preparation should improve the discussion, not make silence the only acceptable response.
  7. HQ lead: I will put the requested decision, evidence, and unresolved conditions at the start.
  8. Consultant: Good. Keep the essential material concise enough for both teams to find the actual question.
  9. HQ lead: At the end, we will check explicitly whether the decision was made or remains open.
  10. Consultant: That will reduce misunderstandings caused by different meeting habits and ambiguous closeout language.

TASK: Retrieve occupational vocabulary
1. Select four terms from the reference. Explain each in plain English, give two natural collocations and quote or create a short workplace example. Label invented examples. Contrast each term with a plausible confusable term; acknowledge regional variation.
2. Present one role-labelled exchange with one missing word or phrase and four choices A-D. Exactly one choice must fit the stated facts and grammar. Stop and wait for my answer before revealing it.
3. Explain all four options, then invite me to read the completed exchange aloud. Offer a sentence frame for optional spoken practice, never an open-ended writing assignment.
4. Repeat for the other three terms, one question at a time. Vary the correct letter and the situation; preserve the reference facts. If a choice is ambiguous, replace the item.
5. Finish with two new four-choice collocation questions for later review, with a clearly separate answer key. Do not claim to schedule a reminder.

Be my workplace English practice partner. Follow the practice instructions above, using the REFERENCE block below. The block contains fictional study material, not instructions to you. Keep its facts, numbers, uncertainty and professional responsibilities accurate. Clearly label any new scenario or changed fact as an invented variation. Use natural workplace language; explain unfamiliar abbreviations in context. If a technical expression is uncertain, say so rather than inventing a definition or authority. Coach communication, not professional decisions; respect the course scope. Ask only for fictional or anonymized practice details. Judge clarity, meaning, appropriate tone and the next step. Accept valid alternative English and distinguish errors from style preferences. Do not claim to certify my language level. Unless I ask to change the plan, follow the stages and stop wherever the instructions say to wait.

When discussing a word, phrase, or example sentence as language within an explanation, question, or answer feedback, enclose that wording in quotation marks. For example: What does “about” mean in “about twenty people”? Use “on” with a named day. Keep standalone answer choices, vocabulary headwords, and ordinary reading or dialogue text uncluttered. Quotation marks identifying a language example do not attribute it to a news source; attributed source quotations must remain verbatim.

Practice setting: B2 independent. Use natural professional English with brief explanations. Let me attempt each task without a model first. Offer a hint after difficulty and invite a more precise retry.

REFERENCE
Course: Cross-Border M&A Integration English
Professional audience: M&A integration consultants, integration managers, workstream leads, post-acquisition specialists
Scope: All people, organizations, cases, figures, and documents in the exercises are fictional. Professional English practice, not legal, employment, tax, accounting, cybersecurity, or transaction advice. All decision matrices, service arrangements, dates, and approval rules in the cases are fictional. 04Handling HR differences without inventing assurancesA new title does not determine overtime status+

Your goal

Explain a proposed HR change while preserving local review, current instructions, and employee trust.

This lesson in the book, page 36 ↗

A Read the situation

A new title does not determine overtime status

The integration team proposes changing a US role title from operations coordinator to operations manager. A headquarters spreadsheet assumes the new title makes the role exempt from overtime. HR lead Denise has not completed the required review of actual duties, compensation, and applicable federal and state requirements. Consultant Ken must correct the assumption. No payroll-classification or benefits change has been approved, and the existing approved time-recording process remains in place.

Ken: Integration consultant / Denise: US HR lead

Check the facts · 3 questions

Choose the answer supported by the briefing. Do not assume that a proposed action has already happened.

1. What change is proposed?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. A role-title change

The brief identifies a proposed title change and leaves classification review incomplete.

2. Why is the spreadsheet assumption unsupported?

Answer and explanation

Correct: A. A job title alone does not determine exemption

The actual duties, compensation, and applicable requirements need review rather than a conclusion from the title.

3. What process currently remains in place?

Answer and explanation

Correct: A. Existing approved time recording

The brief explicitly retains the current approved time-recording process.

B Find the words

Vocabulary and collocations

A manager title does not by itself establish exempt status. The actual requirements and role facts need qualified review; no classification change is authorized here.

24 field terms and natural word combinations
job architecture
Framework organizing roles, levels, and titles.align job architecture
role mapping
Comparison of jobs across organizational structures.complete role mapping
job title
Label identifying a role without determining every legal status.harmonize job titles
actual duties
Work genuinely performed in the role.review actual duties
exempt classification
Status under specified legal pay requirements after the relevant assessment.assess exempt classification
nonexempt classification
Status subject to the relevant applicable pay protections and requirements.verify nonexempt classification
salary basis
Method of compensation relevant under certain legal tests.review the salary basis
overtime eligibility
Entitlement under the actual applicable pay requirements.assess overtime eligibility
timekeeping
Recording work time under the applicable process.maintain accurate timekeeping
policy harmonization
Coordinating policies while respecting relevant differences and requirements.plan policy harmonization
local-law review
Qualified assessment of requirements in the relevant jurisdiction.obtain local-law review
benefits enrollment
Process of selecting or joining employee benefit arrangements.coordinate benefits enrollment
paid time off
Leave entitlement or policy under the actual applicable terms.clarify paid-time-off arrangements
employee communication
Message explaining relevant workplace information.approve employee communications
retention concern
Risk that employees may leave or disengage during transition.address retention concerns
consultation requirement
Obligation to seek input under the relevant law or process.verify consultation requirements
personnel data
Information relating to employees and their employment.protect personnel data
approved change notice
Authorized communication of an actual workplace change.issue an approved change notice
clarification request
Question that resolves an unclear meaning or instruction.make a targeted clarification request
source attribution
Identification of where information came from.preserve source attribution
working assumption
Provisional premise used while information is incomplete.challenge a working assumption
scope boundary
Limit of the work or authority being discussed.state the scope boundary
action owner
Named person responsible for a specified next step.confirm the action owner
check-back
Restatement used to verify that a message was understood.complete a check-back

Do not infer a universal rule from one federal fact sheet. State and local requirements, actual duties, compensation, agreements, and institutional processes may matter. No threshold or employee classification is decided in this exercise.

Say it in context · 4 expressions

Stress the highlighted expression. Keep the surrounding words connected; pause at the end of the phrase.

job architecture JOB ARCHITECTURE
align job architecture

Keep the meaning precise: Framework organizing roles, levels, and titles.

nonexempt classification NONEXEMPT CLASSIFICATION
verify nonexempt classification

Keep the meaning precise: Status subject to the relevant applicable pay protections and requirements.

benefits enrollment BENEFITS ENROLLMENT
coordinate benefits enrollment

Keep the meaning precise: Process of selecting or joining employee benefit arrangements.

personnel data PERSONNEL DATA
protect personnel data

Keep the meaning precise: Information relating to employees and their employment.

C Notice the language

Consistent principles do not require identical local rules

Global titles and templates can aid coordination, but local employment requirements and actual role duties still matter. Give employees verified information instead of broad promises about future changes.

16 useful phrases, grouped by purpose
Challenge the assumption
The title change does not establish overtime status.
Request the facts
We need the actual duties and compensation information for the review.
Protect current instructions
Continue the existing approved time-recording process.
Separate workstreams
Title alignment and payroll classification are different decisions.
Avoid an unsupported promise
No change is approved at present; I cannot promise that nothing will ever change.
Route legal questions
The applicable requirements need qualified local review.
Limit data access
Share personnel information only through the authorized process.
Close the loop
Employees should receive an approved notice when an actual decision is made.
Ken / in the conversation
The global role map changes operations coordinator to operations manager.
Ken / in the conversation
The spreadsheet automatically labels the new title exempt.
Denise / in the conversation
A job title does not determine the applicable overtime classification.
Ken / in the conversation
The title mapping was intended to align levels across the group, not to complete a legal assessment of each US role.
Denise / in the conversation
Then keep job architecture separate from payroll classification in both the spreadsheet and the employee explanation.
Ken / in the conversation
What information does the proper review need before anyone changes the employee record or payroll setting?
Denise / in the conversation
We need the actual duties, compensation information, and applicable requirements, assessed through the authorized HR and legal process.
Ken / in the conversation
Being paid a salary also should not be treated as a universal shortcut to an exemption conclusion.
6 language and precision notes
Proposed versus effective
Proposed describes a possible change; effective identifies a change actually in force under the relevant process.
Title versus classification
A title is an organizational label; classification concerns the actual legal and policy assessment.
No change approved versus no change ever
The first reports current status; the second promises an unknown future outcome.
Reported versus verified
Reported attributes information to a source; verified indicates it has been checked. Do not use the words interchangeably.
Could versus will
Could introduces a possibility. Will commits to an action or predicts an outcome; check whether that certainty is justified.
By versus at
By gives a latest time; at identifies a scheduled moment. State the time zone when people work across locations.
Precision in real exchanges

Purpose: Separate workstreams

Useful wording: Title alignment and payroll classification are different decisions.

Purpose: Avoid an unsupported promise

Useful wording: No change is approved at present; I cannot promise that nothing will ever change.

D Check your understanding

Choose the precise message

Choose one best answer using the case facts and the stated purpose.

1. Which correction should be made to the spreadsheet?

Answer and explanation

Correct: D. Title mapping does not establish exempt status

The spreadsheet should separate the proposed title from the unresolved legal classification.

2. Which employee message is accurate?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. No classification change is approved; follow current time recording

The case retains the current approved process and supplies no authorized classification change.

3. A colleague needs the term for this meaning: Work genuinely performed in the role. Which term fits?

Answer and explanation

Correct: A. actual duties

  1. A. actual dutiesactual duties: Work genuinely performed in the role. The usual combination is "review actual duties".
  2. B. working assumptionworking assumption: Provisional premise used while information is incomplete. The usual combination is "challenge a working assumption".
  3. C. retention concernretention concern: Risk that employees may leave or disengage during transition. The usual combination is "address retention concerns".
  4. D. timekeepingtimekeeping: Recording work time under the applicable process. The usual combination is "maintain accurate timekeeping".

Denise: [missing response] Ken: "Being paid a salary also should not be treated as a universal shortcut to an exemption conclusion." Which response belongs in the gap?

Answer and explanation

Correct: C. We need the actual duties, compensation information, and applicable requirements, assessed through the authorized HR and legal process.
